newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam's son telephones Iraq soccer team.
newsitem.headline: Saddam's son telephones Iraq soccer team.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's eldest son, who was attacked last week by unknown gunmen, telephoned the country's soccer team in Dubai on Sunday to wish them well in the Asian Cup.

Shebab (Youth) television, which is owned by Saddam's eldest son Uday, said in a broadcast: "Uday Saddam Hussein has personally contacted our soccer squad in the (United Arab Emirates) UAE today. He blessed their efforts and told them that he was waiting for good results."
Iraq is now competing in the quarter-finals of the Asian Cup games held in the UAE and on Sunday was playing against the United Arab Emirates.

Uday, 32, was shot at on Thursday evening while driving through Baghdad's posh al-Mansour district, since visited by thousands of Iraqis slaughtering sheep and handing out sweets to celebrate that Uday survived the assault.
He is being treated at Ibn Sina hospital in Baghdad and according to official accounts his wounds are not serious.

Two opposition groups abroad have claimed responsibility for the attack but there has been no official confirmation of the identity odf the gunmen. Iraqi authorities have said they were investigating the incident.
Uday is chairman of Iraq's National Olympic Committee, heads Iraq's Football Federation and owns the newspaper Babel, Iraq's most influential.

Baghdad newspapers on Sunday carried a telegram from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, who congratulated the president on his son's survival and urged Iraq to keep up its backing of the Palestinians.
It was the first reported telegram from an Arab leader to Saddam on the incident.
There has been no official comment on Uday's health since the terse statement by the presidential office on Thursday on the incident.
